reasoning: Recent polling and analysis of the 2026 Ohio Senate special election consistently show Democrat Sherrod Brown holding a small but real lead over Republican Sen. Jon Husted, typically within single digits, while structural factors (R+6 PVI) still favor Republicans. A Fox News poll and several syntheses of multiple polls place Brown up by around 8 points in one high-quality survey but closer to a 1-point edge in polling averages, so the best current read is that the Senate race is leaning D by roughly D+1–2 despite Ohio’s underlying Republican tilt; there is no fresh, high‑quality general‑election presidential polling in the last 45 days specific to Ohio in the provided results, so no current presidential margin can be reliably stated from this data alone.

sources.name: Fox News poll (reported by Washington Examiner)
sources.details: A Fox News/Beacon Research/Shaw poll of Ohio’s 2026 Senate race found Sherrod Brown at 53% and Jon Husted at 45%, an 8-point lead that Fox noted was unchanged from its June poll.

sources.name: PoliticalWire summary of Fox News Ohio Senate poll
sources.details: PoliticalWire summarized a new Fox News poll in Ohio showing Sherrod Brown leading Jon Husted 53% to 45% in the Senate race, matching the previous Fox reading from June.

sources.name: Newsweek coverage of Fox News Ohio Senate poll
sources.details: Newsweek reported on a Fox News poll showing Democrat Sherrod Brown leading Republican Jon Husted 53% to 45% in Ohio’s Senate race, emphasizing it as one of several warning signs for Republicans.

sources.name: G2G Consulting overview of Ohio 2026 Senate polling
sources.details: G2G Consulting described the Ohio Senate race as effectively a toss-up but noted polling averages showing Sherrod Brown with a razor-thin lead of about +0.6 points, with other surveys alternating between slight advantages for each candidate.

sources.name: Idaho Public Press / VoteHub July 2026 Ohio Senate average
sources.details: Idaho Public Press, summarizing VoteHub’s polling averages, said the Ohio Senate race moved from a 0.3-point Republican lead in April to a 0.9-point Democratic lead in July, characterizing Democrats as narrowly ahead.

sources.name: ElectionDesk overview of Ohio Senate special election polling
sources.details: ElectionDesk’s analysis of Ohio’s Senate special election noted that public polling had moved considerably and that recent polls ranged from Brown ahead 47–45 in one Republican-aligned pollster’s survey to Husted up by a point in another, with a mid-June AARP poll putting Brown up 48–45; it concluded no clear favorite had emerged but the race remained very close.

sources.name: The Hill on Wedgewood Poll of Ohio Senate race
sources.details: The Hill reported a Wedgewood Poll showing Sherrod Brown with 48% to Jon Husted’s 44% in the Ohio Senate race, describing Brown’s advantage as a slim lead.

sources.name: Secondary recap of Fox News Ohio Senate poll (Balloon Juice)
sources.details: Balloon Juice cited Fox News Senate polls, listing Ohio as Brown 53% and Husted 45%, an 8-point margin, though this is a secondary reference to the original Fox survey.

sources.name: Daily Kos discussion of Ohio Senate polling
sources.details: Daily Kos commentary on Ohio noted that available polling suggested the Senate race was either a dead heat or that Husted was narrowly ahead, while also saying the environment was shifting against Republicans, reflecting mixed but close polling.

sources.name: Ballotpedia overview of Ohio 2026 state Senate elections
sources.details: Ballotpedia’s Ohio State Senate elections 2026 page provides procedural information about the state’s legislative elections and timing but does not provide or interpret polling in the federal Senate or presidential races.
